back: A curve showing all combinations of two goods that give the consumer equal satisfaction.
The amount of one good a consumer will give up for one more unit of another, staying on the same indifference curve; the slope of the curve (MUx ÷ MUy).
All combinations of two goods affordable with a given income at given prices; slope = PX ÷ PY.

front: What is the **equilibrium condition** in indifference curve analysis?
back: Tangency of the highest affordable indifference curve with the budget line: MRS = PX ÷ PY.

front: What does a change in **income** do to the budget line?
back: A parallel shift (outward if income rises).

front: What does a change in the **price of X** do to the budget line?
back: It pivots on the intercept of the other good; a fall in PX pivots it outward on the X axis.
The change in quantity demanded due to the change in relative prices, keeping the consumer on the original indifference curve.

front: Define the **income effect** of a price change.
back: The change in quantity demanded caused by the change in the consumer's real income.
A very inferior good whose negative income effect outweighs the substitution effect, so a price rise increases quantity demanded.
